plans.note: No dedicated limitation-of-liability heading appears in the supplied outline, but the numbering skips sections 3, 4, 6, 9 and 11, so a cap may sit there or be embedded in the indemnity at sec-12. Check sec-12 for any liability ceiling, consequential-damages waiver and whether it runs both ways; note any cap that protects only TrueLink.

sec-12 (INDEMNITY) is the primary target. Confirm TrueLink indemnifies us for third-party IP infringement in the licensed platform and hosting services and for its own misconduct; watch for a one-way Client indemnity, which would also be foreshadowed by the Client-only covenants in sec-8 and the spam obligations in sec-7.

Restrictions on the businesses Client may operate would most plausibly appear as a licence-scope condition in sec-2 or a Client covenant in sec-8; nothing in the outline signals one. Confirm on read-through before concluding absent.
Check sec-2 for any 'sole provider of Hosting Services' language and sec-8 for a Client covenant not to use competing hosting or licensing platforms; no exclusivity heading is visible.
Any most-favoured-pricing mechanic would sit in sec-5 (COMPENSATION). Only flag if the clause obliges Client to give TrueLink best terms; an MFN running in our favour is welcome and is not redlined.

Employee non-solicits are often tucked into the Client covenants (sec-8) or at the tail of confidentiality (sec-10). If found, test duration, scope and whether general advertising and unsolicited applicants are carved out.

No term/termination heading appears in the supplied outline (sections 3, 4, 6, 9 and 11 are not listed). Look for termination rights in those unlisted sections; also check sec-5 for early-termination fees or unwinding of prepaid amounts.

Auto-renewal and notice windows would normally live in the unlisted term section; sec-5 is the only supplied section likely to carry renewal pricing or uplift language. Verify notice period and whether renewal pricing is capped.

No general/miscellaneous section is supplied; governing law and venue are likely in an unlisted trailing section. Confirm New York, Delaware, California or England and Wales with courts rather than foreign arbitration.

Assignment and change-of-control terms are typically in the boilerplate, which is not in the supplied outline. Confirm we may assign to affiliates and successors and that TrueLink cannot terminate on our change of control.

Test sec-1 definitions (Client, TrueLink, Hosting Services) and sec-2 for any grant-back or vendor ownership of Client content, customer/borrower data or site materials; sec-10 confidentiality may also allocate rights in data. We must own our data and anything we pay for.

sec-2 (LICENSE) is the core clause. Check whether the grant extends to Client affiliates and contractors, and whether it is revocable at will or otherwise conditioned; read with the sec-1 definitions of Hosting Services.

An audit or records-inspection right against Client would most likely be attached to the compensation mechanics in sec-5 or the Client covenants in sec-8. If present, test frequency, notice, on-site scope and who bears cost.

sec-7 (UNSOLICITED COMMERCIAL E-MAIL) is a likely home for per-message penalties or fixed charges against Client; also check sec-5 for late fees or fixed damages. Service credits running to us are welcome and should not be flagged.

sec-8 covers warranties of Client only; a TrueLink performance warranty for the licensed software and Hosting Services may sit in an unlisted section (3, 4, 6 or 9). If none exists, treat as missing and note the asymmetry with sec-8.

No insurance heading in the supplied outline. Given TrueLink hosts our site and handles Client data, an insurance covenant is expected; confirm against the unlisted sections before recording as missing.
Any minimum fee, volume floor or take-or-pay would be in sec-5 (COMPENSATION). If a minimum exists, check for an exit or true-up rather than an unconditional commitment.

No termination or wind-down section is supplied; sec-10 may address return or destruction of confidential information, which is a partial substitute. Confirm whether return of Client data and migration assistance from the Hosting Services is addressed anywhere before recording as missing.
